title: How the queen moves

D0.outcome: Says that the queen moves like a rook and a bishop together.

D1.outcome: When told 'queen', marks every square the queen can move to, stopping in front of its own pieces and at the first enemy piece on each line.

D2.outcome: In a busy position where the piece is not named, marks every square the queen can reach.

D3.outcome: Without a board, says whether the queen reaches a square in one move or needs two, and names a square from which it attacks two lines at once.

misconceptions: The queen can also move like a knight.
Because it is the strongest piece, the queen can safely take anything.
conditions: The queen has the moves of a rook and a bishop from the same square.
Each of its eight lines is blocked separately: a blocker on one line does not affect the others.
contrasts: The queen does not jump like a knight.
A piece blocking the rank does not stop the queen using the file and the diagonals.
